skill.name: html-injection-testing
skill.description: Guidance for authorized HTML injection assessment, including attack surface mapping, payload examples, validation steps, and remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Helps reviewers understand HTML injection testing and defenses, with significant dual-use risk.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, and the innerHTML snippets are documentation examples. However, the skill contains confirmed high-risk phishing, credential capture, defacement, filter-bypass, and active network-testing guidance that makes it unsafe without substantial remediation.

remediation.suggestion: Remove fake login forms, credential capture endpoints, and phishing URL construction. Replace them with non-collecting proof-of-impact descriptions and safe screenshots from authorized labs.
Remove full-page overlays, hacked messaging, misleading account compromise text, and defacement image payloads. Focus on describing impact without enabling public misuse.
Remove bypass payload lists, null-byte tricks, tag splitting, and event-handler examples. Keep high-level remediation guidance for canonicalization and output encoding.

remediation.issue: Active scanning and network request examples
remediation.suggestion: Constrain commands and scripts to local lab targets, include explicit authorization checks, and avoid payloads that send data to external domains.

content.value_statement: HTML injection issues can enable fake content, phishing, and page manipulation. This skill organizes assessment concepts, payload categories, verification steps, and remediation guidance for authorized web security reviews.
actual_capabilities: Explains how HTML injection differs from XSS.
Lists common input surfaces such as search, profile, and form fields.
Provides sample payload categories for reflected and stored injection checks.
Shows browser and proxy based verification workflows.
Includes prevention guidance for escaping, validation, CSP, and sanitization.
Includes a simple fuzzing workflow for authorized targets.
limitations: Does not verify authorization for a target application.
Includes examples that can be misused for phishing or defacement.
Does not replace a full web application security review.
May require manual browser verification after automated checks.

use_cases.title: Review authorized application inputs
use_cases.description: Map reflected and stored injection points, then document impact and remediation.

use_cases.title: Fix unsafe rendering paths
use_cases.description: Use escaping, sanitization, and CSP guidance to reduce injection exposure.

use_cases.title: Assess marketplace safety
use_cases.description: Identify high-risk payloads and dual-use guidance before approving internal training material.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain HTML injection in simple terms for an authorized web application review. Include the difference from XSS and safe remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authorized Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conservative test plan for my authorized staging application. Focus on input surfaces, evidence collection, and safe proof of impact.

prompt_templates.title: Review Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these HTML injection findings from an authorized test. Rank risk, identify likely root causes, and propose remediation steps without adding exploit payloads.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Rendering Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my rendering and templating approach for HTML injection risk. Recommend output encoding, sanitization boundaries, CSP controls, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: A user profile bio renders HTML tags in the public profile page.
output: Finding: stored HTML injection in profile bio.
Impact: content manipulation and possible phishing risk.
Recommended fix: encode untrusted profile fields and add regression tests.

output_examples.input: A search page reflects a styled heading from a query parameter.
output: Finding: reflected HTML injection in search results.
Impact: misleading content in crafted links.
Recommended fix: apply context-aware output encoding for query text.

output_examples.input: A template uses unsafe raw HTML rendering for comments.
output: Finding: unsafe rendering boundary in comment display.
Impact: stored content can alter page structure.
Recommended fix: use escaped rendering by default and allowlist safe formatting.

best_practices: Run tests only on systems where you have written authorization.
Capture minimal proof of impact and avoid collecting credentials or personal data.
Pair every finding with root cause, affected context, and a remediation test.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to create phishing pages, credential capture forms, or public defacement.
Testing production systems without authorization, scope, and rollback planning.
Copying payloads into reports without explaining business impact and remediation.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to publish?
faq.answer: The audit identified high-risk dual-use content and credential theft examples, so publication requires remediation.

faq.question: Does it execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation, but it includes commands and scripts users could run manually.

faq.question: Can it support authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes, only within explicit scope. Unsafe examples should be removed or constrained before publication.

faq.question: How is HTML injection different from XSS?
faq.answer: HTML injection changes page markup. XSS executes script. Both require careful output handling review.

faq.question: Which fixes does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends output encoding, input validation, sanitizer use, CSP, and avoiding unsafe rendering APIs.

faq.question: What should authors change before approval?
faq.answer: Remove phishing, credential capture, defacement, and filter bypass instructions. Refocus the skill on detection and remediation.
